artifacts.name: test_homepage_matches_mockup_story_and_navigation
artifacts.source_scenario: A visitor opens the MAID Runner homepage and scans the product story.

expected.behavior: The homepage exposes the mockup-aligned hero, primary actions, navigation anchors, validation panels, problem cards, and all major page sections with semantic headings.

artifacts.name: test_homepage_renders_workflow_capabilities_tools_and_quickstart
artifacts.source_scenario: A visitor scrolls through the homepage to understand the MAID loop and how to start.

expected.behavior: The page renders seven plan-to-evidence steps, six capability cards, tool compatibility labels, and the documented quick-start commands without suggesting maid verify on an empty repository.

artifacts.name: test_homepage_uses_final_local_brand_and_social_assets
artifacts.source_scenario: A browser and social crawler load the homepage after the disposable design inputs have been consumed.

expected.behavior: Favicon, touch-icon, header/footer logo, and social metadata point to local final assets; every local HTML reference exists; and mockup-redesign.png, logo.png, and social-card-v2.png are absent and unreferenced.

artifacts.name: test_mobile_navigation_covers_javascript_and_no_javascript_paths
artifacts.source_scenario: A visitor uses the compact navigation on a small screen with JavaScript enabled or disabled.

expected.behavior: The script covers open/close, link dismissal, Escape dismissal, and focus return while CSS keeps navigation visible and usable without JavaScript.

artifacts.name: test_dark_surface_accessibility_contract_is_declared
artifacts.source_scenario: A visitor reads and navigates the dark mockup-aligned page across desktop and mobile.

expected.behavior: The stylesheet declares readable text tokens, visible focus states on dark surfaces, responsive rules, and reduced-motion handling.

artifacts.name: test_static_fallback_and_search_metadata_target_canonical_domain
artifacts.source_scenario: A visitor follows a stale Pages URL or a crawler reads deployment metadata.

expected.behavior: 404.html provides a real recovery link and local brand asset, robots.txt points to the canonical sitemap, sitemap.xml is valid XML, and all canonical locations target https://maidrunner.dev/.

artifacts.name: test_pages_workflow_is_path_scoped_and_uploads_website_root
artifacts.source_scenario: A website change lands on main or an operator manually dispatches the Pages workflow.

expected.behavior: The workflow triggers only for main website/workflow changes or manual dispatch, uses least-privilege Pages permissions, uploads website as the artifact root, and deploys through GitHub Pages with immutable action SHAs.

artifacts.name: test_homepage_leads_with_core_strengths
artifacts.source_scenario: A visitor scans the top of the homepage to understand what MAID Runner actually enforces, not just that it 'follows the plan'.

expected.behavior: The page leads with MAID's differentiated strengths -- machine-checkable contracts, tamper-evident planning, portability across agents, and evidence-backed handoff -- frames MAID as governing the artifacts agents produce, and no longer reduces the story to a single follow-the-plan headline in the hero or the social/search metadata.

scope.reason: The static homepage is the mockup implementation surface; its observable structure and copy are covered by the behavioral contract.
The responsive dark visual system and accessibility behavior have no stable programmatic API and are covered by source-level contract assertions plus a browser smoke check.
Progressive-enhancement navigation wiring has no public API; the behavior contract covers open, close, Escape, focus return, and no-JavaScript fallback.
The GitHub Pages fallback document is a static route artifact covered through canonical recovery and brand-asset assertions.
Crawler policy remains part of the canonical static deployment surface.
Search-engine discovery metadata remains part of the canonical static deployment surface.
The final native brand mark is a static asset used by the header, footer, favicon, and touch icon.
The final social preview is a static binary asset referenced by Open Graph and Twitter metadata.
The existing Pages workflow is part of the site contract and remains covered for path scoping, permissions, and artifact-root behavior.
